THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 30, 1935

WHEN MARRIAGE IS UNLAWFUL

Petition for Judicial Separation Dismissed in British Court by Judge A. G. Mossop

"It is hopeless for me to go on unless she is sixteen years of age." This statement was made by Mr. H. A. Reeks in H.M. Supreme Court yesterday morning to Judge A. G. Mossop, who had pointed out to Mr. Reeks that if the petitioner, Claudia Vladimirovna Abbass, was born on December 24, 1918, and married the respondent on May 7, 1934, as stated in her pleadings, then at the time of her marriage she was under sixteen years of age.

In her petition, the petitioner asked for a judicial separation from her lawfully married husband, John Abbass, on the ground of cruelty. The respondent, represented by Mr. Ranald McDonald, in answer to the petition, said that he was not lawfully married to the petitioner and asked that her petition be rejected and that a decree be made that the alleged marriage was null and void.

In his reply filed to the petition the respondent admitted, however, that he had gone through a religious ceremony in the St. Nicolas Russian Orthodox Church, Shanghai, purporting to be a marriage with the petitioner.

After hearing both petition and answer filed to it read out by Mr. Reeks, his Lordship said it was first necessary to show that the petitioner was lawfully married to the respondent on May 7, 1934. He then drew the attention of Mr. Reeks to the fact that the petitioner, according to filed particulars, was under 16 years of age at the time of her marriage. Mr. Reeks intimated that it was an error and actually the petitioner was sixteen years and five months old at the date of her marriage to the respondent. He suggested that the petition be amended.

His Lordship pointed out that the object of particulars was to tie the facts of the case down. He said he must be satisfied or shown authority for changing the particulars in this case. Counsel, after due consideration, said the case must fall as the particulars showed the petitioner under sixteen years of ago.

Case Summed Up

Summing up the whole hearing his Lordship said:—

"This is a suit for judicial separation instituted by the petitioner, Claudia Vladimirovna Abbass, against the respondent, John Abbass. The ground on which the petitioner claims a judicial separation is cruelty, but the respondent in the case, in addition to denying cruelty, denies that the petitioner is now or ever was his legal wife. Paragraph one of the petition states as follows: 'Your petitioner was on May 7, 1934, at the age of sixteen legally married to John Abbass in St. Nicolas Church in Shanghai'."

"The defendant's answer is as follows: The petitioner was not on May 7, 1934 or at all lawfully married to the respondent in St. Nicolas Church in Shanghai or at all. The respondent admits that on May 20, 1934, he went through a religious ceremony purporting to be a marriage with the petitioner in the St. Nicolas Russian Orthodox Church, Shanghai. The said St. Nicolas Russian Orthodox Church is a Russian institution. The petitioner is a Russian. The respondent is a Protestant Christian and a British subject."

"There is therefore in this case a direct issue as to the validity of the marriage. Now under our laws a marriage to be valid must conform to certain requirements. Firstly the parties to the marriage must have the capacity to marry. That capacity is governed by the law of the domicile of each party. Secondly, the manner of carrying out the ceremony must conform to certain requirements of the law."

A Warning Given

His Lordship said that in this case he was for the moment only concerned with the first of the two points, namely the capacity of the parties. It followed, therefore, that anything he had to say should not be interpreted to mean that a British Court would necessarily hold a ceremony of marriage celebrated in St. Nicolas Church in Shanghai not to be a perfectly good marriage. His Lordship said he was not concerned with that point and he did not want any misunderstanding about it.

Continuing his Lordship said: "Now regarding the question of the capacity of the parties this is governed by the law of the domicile of each party. The petitioner is stated to have been a Russian by birth. She was subject to the jurisdiction of the Chinese Courts in China. Article 980 of the Chinese Civil Code lays down: 'A man who has not completed his eighteenth year of age and a woman her sixteenth year of age may not conclude a marriage.' Actually, the Article does not make such a marriage void, but says it may not be precluded."

"Article 989 provides that where a marriage is concluded contrary to the provision of Article 980 the party concerned may apply to the court for its annulment."

The Other Side

"But," his Lordship continued, "there is another side to the picture. The law which governs the respondent John Abbass is the law of England as applied in this court. By an English statute, the Age of Marriage Act, 1929, a marriage between persons either of whom is under the age of sixteen shall be void. Also under English law it is a criminal offence for a man to have carnal knowledge of a female under the age of sixteen. So that the only question is whether the provisions of this act are applicable to the marriage of British subjects in China. I confess that I can see no reason whatever why that provision should not be applied to British subjects in this country under the Order-in-Council."

"The petitioner has, under the order of this court, filed particulars of her case and the first question that was asked of her with regard to paragraph one on the petition was 'What was the date of your birth?' She has filed the particulars in which she says the date of her birth was December 24, 1918. That is supported by an affidavit."

"On the face of her pleadings, therefore, she was on May 7, 1934, aged fifteen years and 134 days. It is because the marriage as far as John Abbass is concerned was void and, as far as she is concerned was a prohibited marriage and voidable, that I have no alternative but to dismiss the petition."

"As regards the question of costs I have to exercise my discretion. I do not know the facts of the case other than the facts disclosed in the pleadings, but, I do know that the petitioner admits having gone through a ceremony of marriage with the respondent. It is difficult to avoid the feeling that, to some extent, he has only got himself to thank for the position in which he finds himself. The petitioner is not subject to the jurisdiction of this court and I do not feel, in the circumstances, that I would be doing the right thing by making her guardian pay the costs of the case."

"Accordingly," he concluded, "there will be no order as to costs."

《字林西报》，1935年10月30日，星期三

当婚姻属非法时

英国法院法官A. G. Mossop驳回司法分居申请

“除非她年满十六岁，否则我继续下去是没有希望的。”H. A. Reeks先生昨天上午在英王陛下最高法院向A. G. Mossop法官作了上述陈述。Mossop法官曾向Reeks先生指出，如果原告Claudia Vladimirovna Abbass如在其诉状中所述，生于1918年12月24日，并于1934年5月7日与被告结婚，那么她在结婚时未满十六岁。

在其申请书中，原告以遭受虐待为由，请求与其合法丈夫John Abbass实行司法分居。被告由Ranald McDonald先生代理，在答辩中表示他并未与原告合法结婚，并请求驳回原告的申请，同时裁定所谓婚姻无效。

然而，被告在提交的答辩状中承认，他曾在上海圣尼古拉俄罗斯东正教堂举行过宗教仪式，该仪式名义上是与原告结婚。

在听取Reeks先生宣读申请书及答辩状后，法官阁下表示，首先必须证明原告于1934年5月7日与被告合法结婚。随后，他提请Reeks先生注意，根据已提交的细节，原告在结婚时未满16岁。Reeks先生暗示这是一个错误，实际上原告在与被告结婚之日为十六岁零五个月。他建议修改申请书。

法官阁下指出，提交案件细节的目的在于确定案件事实。他说，他必须得到满足或看到在此案中更改细节的依据。律师经慎重考虑后表示，鉴于细节显示原告未满十六岁，本案必须败诉。

案件总结

法官阁下在总结整个听证过程时说：—

“这是由原告Claudia Vladimirovna Abbass针对被告John Abbass提起的司法分居诉讼。原告主张司法分居的理由是虐待，但本案被告除了否认虐待外，还否认原告现在或曾经是他的合法妻子。申请书第一段陈述如下：‘您的申请人于1934年5月7日，年满十六岁时，在上海圣尼古拉教堂与John Abbass合法结婚’。”

“被告的答辩如下：原告于1934年5月7日或任何时间均未在上海圣尼古拉教堂或与任何人合法嫁给被告。被告承认，他于1934年5月20日在上海圣尼古拉俄罗斯东正教堂举行了一场名义上与原告结婚的宗教仪式。上述圣尼古拉俄罗斯东正教堂是一个俄罗斯机构。原告是俄罗斯人。被告是新教基督徒且为英国臣民。”

“因此，本案中存在关于婚姻有效性的直接争议。根据我们的法律，有效的婚姻必须符合某些要求。首先，婚姻双方必须具备结婚能力。这种能力受各方住所地法律的管辖。其次，举行仪式的方式必须符合法律的某些要求。”

发出警告

法官阁下说，在本案中，他目前只关注两点中的第一点，即双方的能力。因此，他的任何言论都不应被解释为意味着英国法院必然认定在上海圣尼古拉教堂举行的结婚仪式不是完全有效的婚姻。法官阁下表示，他不关心那一点，也不希望对此产生任何误解。

法官阁下继续说道：“现在关于双方能力的问题，这受各方住所地法律的管辖。据称原告出生时为俄罗斯人。她在中国受中国法院的管辖。《中华民国民法典》第980条规定：‘男未满十八岁，女未满十六岁者，不得结婚。’实际上，该条款并未使此类婚姻无效，而是规定其不得缔结。”

“第989条规定，违反第980条规定缔结婚姻的，有关当事人可以向法院申请撤销。”

另一方面

“但是，”法官阁下继续说，“情况还有另一面。管辖被告John Abbass的法律是本庭适用的英国法律。根据英国1929年《结婚年龄法》，任何一方未满十六岁的婚姻均为无效。此外，根据英国法律，男子与未满十六岁的女子发生性关系属于刑事犯罪。因此，唯一的问题是该法案的规定是否适用于在华英国臣民的婚姻。我承认，我看不到有任何理由不根据《枢密院令》将这一规定适用于在本国的英国臣民。”

“根据本庭命令，原告已提交其案件的细节，就申请书第一段向她提出的第一个问题是‘你的出生日期是什么？’她提交的细节中称其出生日期为1918年12月24日。这一点有宣誓书支持。”

“因此，从其诉状表面来看，她在1934年5月7日时为十五岁零134天。正因为就John Abbass而言该婚姻无效，而就她而言该婚姻属于被禁止且可撤销的婚姻，我别无选择，只能驳回申请。”

“关于诉讼费问题，我必须行使我的裁量权。除了诉状中披露的事实外，我不了解本案的其他事实，但是，我知道原告承认曾与被告举行过结婚仪式。很难避免这样一种感觉，即在某种程度上，他目前的处境只能怪他自己。原告不受本庭管辖，在这种情况下，我觉得让她的监护人支付本案诉讼费并非恰当之举。”

“因此，”他总结道，“不对诉讼费作出裁定。”
